title: DR1 lets the user add a commercial transporter that is not already in the directory; on the frontend a commercial transporter can only be picked from a fixed list, so an unlisted one cannot be used at all.

finding.frontend: Choosing "Commercial" leads to a list of approved commercial transporters and nothing else. There is no "Add" control on that page and no route to one — the transporter part of the transport feature holds exactly three pages: the type question, the commercial pick-list and the private-transporter form (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/transport/page.js:11-25). The list itself is a fixed pair of records held in the frontend (src/server/app/services/commercial-transporters/records.js:6-27). A user whose commercial transporter is not in the list is stuck: the only way onward is to declare the transporter private, which is a different answer to a different question.
finding.prototype: The transporter directory carries an "Add a transporter" secondary button below the list (app/views/transporter.html:160-165). It leads to "Choose a transporter type", warning "Before you add this transporter, please ensure you have already searched for it first" and offering Private transporter or Commercial, where Commercial is hinted "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland". Choosing Commercial gives an "Add commercial transporter" page holding: an "Important — Help with transporter authorisation" panel repeating the DAERA/APHA authorisation rules; Transporter authorisation number; Name or organisation name; Address line 1; Address line 2 (optional); Town or city; County (optional); Postcode or Zip code; Country, which is locked to Northern Ireland and cannot be changed; then under an "Enter contact details" heading, Email address and Phone number. The added transporter joins the directory with the "New" status the list shows.
finding.difference: Build the add-a-transporter branch: an "Add a transporter" button on the commercial list, the type question as a branch of that button rather than as the section's entry, and an "Add commercial transporter" page carrying the fields above. The private form the frontend already has answers DR1's private branch. This depends on the transporter list becoming something a user can add to rather than a fixed list in the frontend, which is the same dependency as the "New" status tag. It also depends on the finding about where the type question sits, because DR1's add journey starts from the directory. One detail of DR1's page must not be copied without asking first: DR1 locks the new transporter's country to Northern Ireland and hints "This can only be a commercial transporter from Northern Ireland", yet the directory that page adds to already holds commercial transporters from Romania, the Republic of Ireland, Denmark and Portugal — transporters that page could never have created. Build the page with an ordinary country field until a designer settles which of the two DR1 means.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a route in the frontend that reaches a form for entering a commercial transporter by hand — the transport feature declares only port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, transporters/select and transporters/private.
finding.verification: Read the frontend page.js and records.js in full, listed the transport feature directory, read all four screens' rendered DOM, and opened the dr1-transporter, dr1-transporter-add and dr1-transporter-add-commercial screenshots. Ran the falsifier: the feature tree holds only port-of-entry, transit-countries, transporters, transporters-select and private-transporter-details, with no add controller or view, so it does not fire. Every field the prototype slot enumerates for "Add commercial transporter" is visible in the screenshot in the order given, including the greyed Country select reading "Northern Ireland", and the warning and hints on "Choose a transporter type" are verbatim. Rubric 2 fired once and rubric 7 fired on one detail. Rubric 2: the frontend slot said "the transport feature holds exactly three pages" while the finding's own falsifiedBy names five; corrected to "the transporter part of the transport feature". Rubric 7: the Northern Ireland country lock is contradicted by DR1's own directory, so finding.difference no longer instructs the frontend to copy it. Everything else CORRECT.
finding.correction: Claimed, in finding.frontend: "the transport feature holds exactly three pages". True: page.js declares five — portOfEntryPage, transitCountriesPage, transportersPage, transportersSelectPage and privateTransporterDetailsPage — three of which are the transporter pages the sentence goes on to name. The finding's own falsifiedBy already said five, so the two slots disagreed. Checked by reading page.js whole and listing features/transport/. Slot fixed. Second, claimed in finding.difference: build the add page "with the country fixed to Northern Ireland". True as a description of DR1's page, but DR1 contradicts itself on it: app/data/transporters.js holds Yusen Logistics (Romania) SRL, Roadtrain Ltd (Dublin), Danish Meat Export ApS and Portuguese Livestock Lda, all typed Commercial, all in the same directory that page adds to. Checked by reading app/data/transporters.js against the hint text captured on dr1-transporter-add. The instruction to lock the field has been replaced by an ordinary country field and the contradiction named; the finding as a whole stands as frontend-work, because the absence of any add route at all is not in doubt.

relatedTo.why: DR1's add journey hangs off the directory, so the type question has to move first
the "New" status tag only means something once a transporter can be added
